memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Iron-deficiency anemia with gastro-oesophageal reflux disease.
Patient reports fatigue, pallor, occasional heartburn after meals, and mild epigastric discomfort. On examination: pallor noted, mild epigastric tenderness, no hepatosplenomegaly, vitals stable.
Smoking status: never smoked, pack-years 0.
Plan: start ferrous sulfate 200 mg OD, pantoprazole 40 mg OD before breakfast, antacid gel SOS, domperidone 10 mg BD before meals. Review in 3 months with labs.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Haemoglobin: 9.8 g/dL (13.0-17.0)
Serum ferritin: 12 ng/mL (30-400)
MCV: 68 fL (80-100)

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been taking the iron tablets but my stomach feels a bit upset after breakfast. The heartburn is better with the pantoprazole, though I still need antacid after spicy meals.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Iron-deficiency anemia improving, gastro-oesophageal reflux controlled.
Patient feels less fatigued, occasional heartburn only after spicy food, no epigastric pain. Examination: pallor markedly improved, abdomen soft, no tenderness.
Smoking status: never smoked, pack-years 0.
Plan: continue ferrous sulfate 200 mg OD, pantoprazole 40 mg OD, consider switching iron to alternate days if ferritin normalizes. Review in 3 months.
